lessons.title: Cé agus Cad é
lessons.rule: Cé (who) and Cad é (what) are followed by a and h on the verb: Cé a bhris an fhuinneog? Cad é a dhéanann tú? For bí in the present, use atá: Cé atá ann? Cad é atá ort?
steps: Start with Cé or Cad é.
Add a, and put h on the verb: cuir becomes a chuir.
For bí in the present, write atá instead: Cé atá ag caint?

example.prompt: (Cé / cuir, an aimsir chaite) glaoch ort aréir?
example.answer: Cé a chuir glaoch ort aréir?

lessons.hint: Cé or Cad é, then a + h. Bí in the present: atá.

lessons.title: Cá + urú
lessons.rule: Cá (where) eclipses the verb after it: Cá bhfuil tú? Cá dtéann tú? In the past, irregular verbs keep Cá with eclipsis (Cá ndeachaigh tú? Cá bhfaca tú é?), but raibh never changes (Cá raibh tú?). Regular verbs in the past take Cár and h: Cár fhág tú do mhála?
steps: Start with Cá.
Eclipse the verb: téann becomes dtéann, imríonn becomes n-imríonn.
In the past, a regular verb takes Cár and h: Cár fhág tú é?

example.prompt: (Cá / imir, an aimsir láithreach) tú peil?

lessons.hint: Cá + eclipsis. Regular past: Cár + h.

lessons.title: Cá háit agus Cén áit
lessons.en: Where: Cá háit and Cén áit
lessons.rule: Cá háit and Cén áit (what place) are followed by a and eclipsis in the present and future: Cá háit a bhfuil sé? Cén áit a mbeidh tú? In the past, irregular verbs take a and eclipsis (Cá háit a ndeachaigh tú?), and regular verbs take ar and h (Cén áit ar fhan tú?).
steps: Start with Cá háit or Cén áit.
Add a and eclipse the verb: a bhfuil, a n-oibríonn.
In the past, a regular verb takes ar and h: Cén áit ar chas tú air?

example.prompt: Cén áit (imir, an aimsir láithreach) sibh peil?
example.answer: Cén áit a n-imríonn sibh peil?

more.prompt: Cén áit (fan, an aimsir chaite) sibh an samhradh seo caite?
more.answer: Cén áit ar fhan sibh an samhradh seo caite?

lessons.hint: a + eclipsis. Regular past: ar + h.

lessons.title: Cad chuige agus Cén fáth
lessons.rule: Cad chuige and Cén fáth (why) are followed by a and eclipsis: Cad chuige a bhfuil tú déanach? Cén fáth a n-imríonn tú camógaíocht? In the past, irregular verbs take a and eclipsis (Cén fáth a ndearna tú sin?), and regular verbs take ar and h (Cad chuige ar chaill tú an bus?).
steps: Start with Cad chuige or Cén fáth.
Add a and eclipse the verb: a bhfuil, a n-imríonn.
In the past, a regular verb takes ar and h: Cad chuige ar fhág tú?

example.answer: Cad chuige a bhfuil tú tuirseach?

lessons.title: Cá mhéad
lessons.rule: Cá mhéad (how many) takes the noun in the singular, not the plural: Cá mhéad deartháir atá agat? Cá mhéad ábhar a dhéanann tú? After the noun, use atá for bí, or a and h for other verbs.
steps: Start with Cá mhéad.
Put the noun in the singular: deartháireacha becomes deartháir.
Add atá, or a and h on the verb: Cá mhéad deartháir atá agat?

more.answer: Cá mhéad leabhar a léigh tú?

lessons.title: Cén + ainmfhocal
lessons.rule: Cén (which, what) changes the noun like the article an: h on a feminine noun (Cén bhliain? Cén mhí?) and t- before a masculine noun beginning with a vowel (Cén t-am? Cén t-ábhar?). Other nouns do not change: Cén lá? Cén aois? Cén obair?
steps: Decide if the noun is masculine or feminine.
Feminine: add h (bliain becomes bhliain). Masculine with a vowel: add t- (am becomes t-am).
Anything else stays as it is: Cén lá?
lessons.hint: Cén works like an: h on feminine nouns, t- on masculine vowels.

items.answer: Cén t-am é?

lessons.title: Cad é mar agus Cén dóigh
lessons.rule: Cad é mar (how) is followed by atá for bí, or a and h: Cad é mar atá tú? Cad é mar a bhí an aimsir? Cén dóigh (in what way) is followed by a and eclipsis: Cén dóigh a bhfuil tú? Cén dóigh a dtéann tú ar scoil?
steps: Cad é mar: atá, or a + h on the verb.
Cén dóigh: a + eclipsis on the verb.
Both are everyday Ulster greetings: Cad é mar atá tú? Cén dóigh a bhfuil tú?

example.answer: Cad é mar atá do mháthair?

lessons.hint: Cad é mar + a + h. Cén dóigh + a + eclipsis.
